All Flink Scala APIs are deprecated and will be removed in a future Flink version. You can still build your application in Scala, but you should move to the Java version of either the DataStream and/or Table API.

See FLIP-265 Deprecate and remove Scala API support

Java

We will now give an overview of each of those steps, please refer to the
respective sections for more details. Note that all core classes of the Java
DataStream API can be found in

org.apache.flink.streaming.api

.

The `StreamExecutionEnvironment` is the basis for all Flink programs. You can
obtain one using these static methods on `StreamExecutionEnvironment`:

```
getExecutionEnvironment();

createLocalEnvironment();

createRemoteEnvironment(String host, int port, String... jarFiles);

```

For specifying data sources the execution environment has several methods to
read from files using various methods: you can just read them line by line, as
CSV files, or using any of the other provided sources. To just read a text file
as a sequence of lines, you can use:

```
final StreamExecutionEnvironment env = StreamExecutionEnvironment.getExecutionEnvironment();

DataStream<String> text = env.readTextFile("file:///path/to/file");

```

This will give you a DataStream on which you can then apply transformations to create new
derived DataStreams.

You apply transformations by calling methods on DataStream with a
transformation functions. For example, a map transformation looks like this:

```
DataStream<String> input = ...;

DataStream<Integer> parsed = input.map(new MapFunction<String, Integer>() {
    @Override
    public Integer map(String value) {
        return Integer.parseInt(value);
    }
});

```

This will create a new DataStream by converting every String in the original
collection to an Integer.

Once you have a DataStream containing your final results, you can write it to
an outside system by creating a sink. These are just some example methods for
creating a sink:

```
writeAsText(String path);

print();

```

skill_drafts.name: Initialize Flink Streaming Execution Environment
skill_drafts.description: Obtain and configure a StreamExecutionEnvironment instance as the foundation for all Flink DataStream programs. This micro-skill establishes the execution context before defining data sources and transformations.
applicable_signals: No prior StreamExecutionEnvironment instance in scope
contraindications: Environment is already initialized in the current program scope
Attempting to reinitialize within the same execution context
workflow_steps: {'step': 1, 'action': 'Determine execution mode', 'detail': 'Decide whether to use automatic detection, local execution, or remote cluster execution'}
{'step': 2, 'action': 'Call appropriate factory method', 'detail': 'Invoke getExecutionEnvironment(), createLocalEnvironment(), or createRemoteEnvironment(host, port, jarFiles)'}
{'step': 3, 'action': 'Store environment instance', 'detail': 'Assign the returned StreamExecutionEnvironment to a variable for use in subsequent operations'}
triggers: Starting a new Flink DataStream application
Switching between local and remote execution modes
Beginning a new program scope that requires independent execution context
constraints: Must be called before defining any data sources or transformations
Only one active StreamExecutionEnvironment per program scope
For remote execution, host and port must be reachable
cautions: Scala API is deprecated; use Java DataStream API instead
Core classes are located in org.apache.flink.streaming.api (Java) or org.apache.flink.streaming.api.scala (Scala, deprecated)
output_contract: A valid, non-null StreamExecutionEnvironment instance ready to accept data source definitions (readTextFile, etc.) and transformation operations (map, filter, etc.).

examples.notes: Environment adapts to execution context (local or cluster)

examples.input: Remote cluster execution with host and port

metadata.prompt: Call one of the static factory methods on StreamExecutionEnvironment to obtain an instance. Choose the method based on your execution mode: getExecutionEnvironment() for automatic mode detection, createLocalEnvironment() for local/embedded execution, or createRemoteEnvironment() for remote cluster execution. Store the returned instance for use in subsequent data source and transformation definitions.

skill_drafts.name: Read Text File as DataStream
skill_drafts.description: Read a text file line-by-line and create a DataStream<String> from it using the StreamExecutionEnvironment. Use this to ingest text-based data sources into the streaming pipeline.
skill_drafts.objective: Ingest text file data into a DataStream
applicable_signals: Data source is a text file
contraindications: Data source is not a text file
Structured parsing (CSV, JSON) is required beyond line-by-line reading
workflow_steps: Obtain or initialize a StreamExecutionEnvironment instance
Call readTextFile(String path) with the file path
Apply downstream transformations or sinks as needed
triggers: Text file is available as a data source
Need to create a DataStream from file-based input
constraints: File path must be accessible to the Flink runtime
File must be readable as text (UTF-8 or compatible encoding)
Each line becomes one DataStream element
cautions: Large files may cause memory pressure; consider partitioning or streaming from external sources
File path format must be valid (e.g., file:/// for local, hdfs:// for HDFS)
output_contract: Returns a DataStream<String> object containing all lines from the file, ready for downstream transformations or sinks. Each line is one element in the stream.

examples.notes: Basic usage; file is read line-by-line and each line becomes a stream element

metadata.prompt: Call readTextFile() on a StreamExecutionEnvironment instance with a file path. The method returns a DataStream<String> where each element is one line from the file. Use this as the entry point for text-based data ingestion in Flink streaming applications.

skill_drafts.name: Apply Map Transformation to DataStream
skill_drafts.description: Transform each element in a DataStream using a MapFunction to produce a new DataStream with converted or derived values. Use this for element-wise transformations such as type conversion or field extraction.
applicable_signals: Need to convert or transform each element in a DataStream independently
Parsing strings to integers or other types
Applying a function to every element with 1:1 cardinality
contraindications: Do not use for filtering elements; use filter() instead
Do not use for aggregating or reducing across elements; use reduce() or aggregate() instead
Do not use for stateful operations; use process functions or state backends instead
Do not use for windowing operations; use window() instead
workflow_steps: {'step': 1, 'action': 'Obtain or create a DataStream instance', 'detail': 'Use StreamExecutionEnvironment methods such as readTextFile() or other source methods'}
{'step': 2, 'action': 'Call map() method on the DataStream', 'detail': 'Pass a MapFunction implementation or lambda expression'}
{'step': 3, 'action': 'Implement the map(T value) method', 'detail': 'Define the transformation logic; receive one input element, return one output element'}
{'step': 4, 'action': 'Assign the result to a new DataStream variable', 'detail': 'The returned DataStream contains the transformed elements'}
triggers: You need to convert or transform each element in a DataStream independently (e.g., parsing strings to integers, extracting fields).
constraints: Input and output types must be compatible with Flink's type system
Transformation must be deterministic and side-effect free for correct distributed execution
cautions: Map maintains 1:1 cardinality; each input element produces exactly one output element
Avoid heavy computations in map; consider async I/O for blocking operations
Ensure the MapFunction implementation is thread-safe if shared across partitions
output_contract: A new DataStream with transformed elements of the target type, maintaining the same cardinality (1:1) as the input stream. Each input element produces exactly one output element.

examples.output: DataStream<Integer> parsed = text.map(new MapFunction<String, Integer>() { @Override public Integer map(String value) { return Integer.parseInt(value); } });
examples.notes: Converts each line (String) to an Integer by parsing

metadata.prompt: Call the map() method on a DataStream with a MapFunction implementation. Override the map(T value) method to define the transformation logic for each element. The function receives one input element and returns one output element of the target type.

skill_drafts.name: Write DataStream to External Sink
skill_drafts.description: Output the final DataStream to an external system (file, console, or custom sink) to persist or display results. Use this as the terminal operation in a Flink pipeline.
skill_drafts.objective: Output stream results to external system
contraindications: Output destination is unavailable or unspecified
workflow_steps: {'step': 1, 'action': 'Verify DataStream is final', 'detail': 'Confirm all transformations have been applied and the DataStream contains the desired output'}
{'step': 2, 'action': 'Select sink method', 'detail': 'Choose writeAsText(path) for file output, print() for console, or custom sink for specialized systems'}
{'step': 3, 'action': 'Invoke sink operation', 'detail': 'Call the selected sink method on the DataStream object'}
{'step': 4, 'action': 'Execute pipeline', 'detail': 'Call env.execute() to trigger the Flink job and write results to the sink'}
triggers: Final DataStream is ready for output
Results need to be persisted or displayed
constraints: Sink operation must be the terminal operation in the pipeline
Output destination must be accessible and writable
Sink method must match the target system type
cautions: Sinking is a blocking terminal operation; ensure all upstream transformations are complete
File-based sinks require valid file paths and write permissions
Console output (print) may impact performance in high-throughput scenarios
output_contract: Results successfully written to the specified sink destination (file, console, or external system); pipeline execution completes without errors; output is persisted or displayed as intended

examples.notes: Output stream to console for verification

metadata.prompt: Apply a sink operation to write the final DataStream to an external destination. Choose the appropriate sink method based on your output target: writeAsText() for file output, print() for console output, or a custom sink for specialized systems. Ensure all transformations are complete before sinking.
